events.title: Pope Paschal II crowns Henry V emperor under duress
events.description: Having held the Pope captive for two months, Henry V forced him to concede the right of investiture and crown him in Rome. The concession was soon revoked, and the dispute lasted until 1122.

events.title: Henry IV signs the Edict of Nantes
events.description: Henry IV granted French Protestants freedom of worship in specified places, civil rights and fortified towns. The edict ended the Wars of Religion until Louis XIV revoked it in 1685.

events.title: Handel's Messiah has its premiere in Dublin
events.description: Handel's oratorio was first performed at the New Music Hall in Fishamble Street, Dublin, in aid of charity. It became one of the most performed choral works in the Western tradition.
events.html: Handel's oratorio was first performed at the New Music Hall in Fishamble Street, Dublin, in aid of charity. It became one of the most performed choral works in the Western tradition.

events.title: Catholic Relief Act receives royal assent
events.description: The Roman Catholic Relief Act allowed Catholics to sit in Parliament and hold most public offices. It was forced through by Wellington and Peel after Daniel O'Connell's election in County Clare.

events.title: Troops fire on a crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar
events.description: Soldiers under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired without warning into an unarmed crowd in an enclosed garden. At least 379 were killed by official count; the massacre hardened Indian opposition to British rule.
events.html: Soldiers under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired without warning into an unarmed crowd in an enclosed garden. At least 379 were killed by official count; the massacre hardened Indian opposition to British rule.

events.title: Germany announces discovery of the Katyń graves
events.description: Berlin radio reported mass graves of Polish officers in the Katyń Forest near Smolensk. They had been shot by the Soviet NKVD in 1940, a crime Moscow denied until 1990.
